mainTopic: Immersing to eat תרומת חוצה לארץ, and how the year and eating time of a בכור are learned
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about a טמא מת. Someone asks how immersion could help when there is no הזאה with the ashes of the פרה אדומה. רמי בר חמא suggests waiting for the elder, רב עמרם. When רב עמרם arrives, he reports that רב allowed a טמא מת to immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ. The גמרא rules that the הלכה does not follow this. It also rejects רב ששת's similar ruling about a טמא שרץ. Then the גמרא returns to the משנה that a בכור is eaten שנה בשנה. From the משנה's wording it shows that the year is counted from the animal's birth, and רב learns this from the words 'שנה בשנה'. דבי רב read the same words as teaching that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night. The גמרא then shows where each side learns the other rule: דבי רב learn the year from other קדשים ('כבש בן שנתו'), and רב learns the two days and one night from a הקש to the חזה ושוק of שלמים.

steps.title: How can immersion help without sprinkling?
steps.stepSummary: Someone challenges the ruling that a טמא מת can immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ, since without הזאה he stays impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we even have sprinkling of the red heifer ashes nowadays?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone attacks the ruling just stated by asking how a טמא מת could become pure by immersing. Without הזאה, corpse impurity does not go away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing טומאת מת takes two things: הזאה with the ashes of the פרה אדומה and then טבילה. Since there is no הזאה available, immersion alone seems useless. So how can this person eat תרומה?

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling of water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה, needed to remove corpse impurity
'But is it so that...?', a phrase that opens a challenge

phrases.english: But do we have sprinkling?
phrases.notes: He means the sprinkling with the פרה אדומה ashes. Without it, corpse impurity never fully leaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling stated just before this section, that a טמא מת may immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a טמא מת may immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Immersion cannot remove טומאת מת without הזאה, and we have no הזאה. So immersion should accomplish nothing.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא suggests waiting for the elder
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא suggests they should take into account the view of the elder, רב עמרם, before settling the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said to him: Shouldn't he be concerned for the opinion of the old man?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא does not answer the challenge directly. He suggests they hear from the elder, רב עמרם, first. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The response is about procedure, not about the law itself. The elder may have a tradition on this question, so it is better to hear it before deciding.

keyTerms.meaning: Should he not be concerned for / take into account
The old man, a respectful way to refer to an elder scholar

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said to him:
Shouldn't he be concerned for the old man?
phrases.notes: The 'old man' is רב עמרם, who had stepped out and is about to come back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Does not answer the challenge. It suggests waiting for the elder's view, which comes in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No direct answer yet. The suggestion is to wait for רב עמרם's opinion.

steps.title: רב עמרם reports רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם arrives and reports that רב ruled a טמא מת may immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, רב עמרם came. He said to them: This is what רב says: One impure from a corpse may immerse and eat תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם comes back and brings a tradition from רב. It supports the lenient ruling that a טמא מת can immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though there is no הזאה, רב allowed immersion alone to be enough for this kind of תרומה. The challenge from Step 1 is answered by an authoritative tradition, not by an argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile, in the middle of this
A person made impure by a corpse
Immerses in a מקוה
תרומה from produce grown outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Meanwhile, Rav Amram came.
He said to them: This is what Rav says:
One impure from a corpse may immerse and eat
teruma from outside the Land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fulfills רמי בר חמא's suggestion: the elder arrives and gives his tradition, which answers the challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ruled that a טמא מת may immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ, even without הזאה.

steps.title: The halacha does not follow this ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה does not follow the lenient ruling reported in רב's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the הלכה is not in accordance with his opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its practical ruling: we do not follow the lenient view that a טמא מת may immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling has a source, but it is not accepted as practical הלכה. So a טמא מת does not eat תרומת חוצה לארץ just by immersing.

keyTerms.meaning: But the הלכה is not like him

phrases.english: But the halacha is not in accordance with his opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final practical ruling on the tradition reported in Step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, a טמא מת does not eat תרומת חוצה לארץ by immersing alone.

steps.title: A similar ruling about one impure from a creeping animal
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, quoting רב ששת, rules that a טמא שרץ may immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ, and the גמרא again says the הלכה does not follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said in the name of רב ששת: One impure from a creeping animal may immerse and eat תרומה from outside ארץ ישראל. But the הלכה is not in accordance with his opinion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, similar lenient ruling about someone who touched a dead שרץ. It then states that this one is also not the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the person is impure from a שרץ, a kind of impurity that does not need הזאה. Even so, the גמרא rejects this lenient ruling in practice as well, just like the one about טמא מת.

keyTerms.meaning: A person made impure by touching the carcass of a creeping animal
In the name of

steps.whatToRemember: Two lenient rulings were stated about immersing and eating תרומת חוצה לארץ, one for טמא מת and one for טמא שרץ. The גמרא says the הלכה follows neither one.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: For Mar Zutra said in the name of Rav Sheshet:
One impure from a creeping animal may immerse and eat
teruma from outside the Land,
but the halacha is not in accordance with his opinion.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel lenient ruling about a different impurity and rejects it in the same way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת: a טמא שרץ may immerse and eat תרומת חוצה לארץ. The גמרא adds that the הלכה does not follow this.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a בכור is eaten שנה בשנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The firstborn is eaten year by year, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה about how long a בכור may be eaten. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that a בכור is eaten within its first year. The next steps look closely at how that year is counted.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, given to the כהן
Year by year, meaning within its first year
Etc., showing the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: The firstborn is eaten year by year, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תרומה discussion and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור may be eaten within its first year.

steps.title: The year is counted from the animal's birth
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's words 'within its year', the גמרא infers that the year is counted from the בכור's own birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the fact that it says 'a blemish developed within its year', that is to say that we count by its own year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה's wording closely. 'Its year' shows that the animal's own year is meant, not the calendar year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have said 'within the year'. Instead it says 'within its year'. That small word 'its' shows the count starts from the day the animal was born.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it says
A blemish that disqualifies an animal from the מזבח
That is to say, an inference is being drawn
We count

phrases.english: From the fact that it says: 'A blemish developed within its year,'
that is to say that we count by its own year.
phrases.notes: 'Its own year' means twelve months from the animal's birth, not the calendar year.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר נוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a precise rule from the wording of the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The year of a בכור is counted from its birth.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the year is counted from the animal's birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we learn that a בכור's year is its own year. This sets up the source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 showed what the משנה holds, but not why. The גמרא now wants the basis in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived? A request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the inference in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that a בכור's year is counted from its birth.

steps.title: רב derives it from 'year in a year'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, explains that 'שנה בשנה' describes a year that runs into the next year, which can only be the year of the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said that רב said: The verse says, 'You shall eat it before the Lord your God year by year.' Which year enters into the next one? You must say: the year of the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source from the פסוק. The words 'שנה בשנה' point to a year that spills over into the next year, and that fits the בכור's own year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שנה בשנה' can be read as 'a year inside a year', meaning one year that runs into another. A calendar year never runs into the next one. A בכור born in the middle of the year has a year that continues into the next calendar year. So the פסוק is talking about the animal's own year.

keyTerms.meaning: As the פסוק says
Enters into its fellow, meaning one year running into the next
You must say, the only possible answer

steps.whatToRemember: A בכור may be eaten for a full year counted from its birth, even when that year runs into the next calendar year. The source is 'שנה בשנה'.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
For the verse says:
"Before the Lord your God you shall eat it
year by year."
Which year enters into its fellow year?
phrases.notes: He is reading 'שנה בשנה' as 'a year in a year', one year running into the next.

phrases.english: You must say: the year of the firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source with a reading of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'שנה בשנה' describes a year that runs into the next year. Only the בכור's own year, counted from its birth, does that.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical deadline for eating a בכור: twelve months from its birth, not the end of the calendar year.

steps.title: The school of רב reads 'year by year' differently
steps.stepSummary: דבי רב teach that 'שנה בשנה' means one day in this year and one day in the next. This teaches that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב taught: 'Year by year' means one day in this year and one day in the next year. This teaches that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different way to read the same words 'שנה בשנה', taught in the study hall of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, רב read 'שנה בשנה' as telling us that the year is counted from the בכור's birth. דבי רב read it as being about how long the meat may be eaten. If the animal is slaughtered on the last day of one year, it can still be eaten on the first day of the next year, which makes two days and the one night between them.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall (school) of רב
Taught (introduces a teaching)
It taught; the פסוק comes to teach
Two days and one night, the eating time of שלמים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב with דבי רב. Here they use the same words 'שנה בשנה' to teach two different things.

phrases.english: The school of Rav taught:
"Year by year" means
one day in this year,
and one day in that year,
phrases.notes: It literally says 'this year' both times, but here it means the next year: slaughter on the last day of one year, finish eating on the first day of the next.

phrases.english: it taught about the firstborn
that it is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same phrase that רב explained in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור is eaten for two days and one night, learned from 'שנה בשנה'

steps.title: Where does the school of רב learn the counting of the year?
steps.stepSummary: Since דבי רב used 'שנה בשנה' for the eating time, the גמרא asks for their source that the year is counted from the animal's birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב: from where do they learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next step. דבי רב 'used up' the פסוק, so where do they get the rule that the year follows the animal's birth?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the בכור's year is counted from its birth. רב learned that from 'שנה בשנה'. Since דבי רב read those words differently, they need another source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do they know it?

phrases.english: The school of Rav, from where do they derive it?
phrases.notes: He means: from where do they know that the year is counted from the בכור's own birth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks where the view in step 10 gets the rule that רב took from the same פסוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source, according to דבי רב, that the בכור's year is counted from its birth

steps.title: They learn it from other sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: דבי רב learn the counting of the year from the rule for other קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from other sacrifices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that דבי רב compare the בכור to other sacrifices, whose age is counted from their birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With other קדשים, the age of the animal (for example 'one year old') is counted from when it was born, not by the calendar. דבי רב apply the same rule to the בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: They learn (derive)
Sacrifices, holy offerings

phrases.english: They derive it from sacrifices.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בכור's year follows the rule of other קדשים, which are counted from birth

steps.title: Where do we learn this about sacrifices themselves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back one more level and asks how we know that the age of other קדשים is counted from their birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the sacrifices themselves: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question and sets up the next step. If the בכור learns from קדשים, what is the source for קדשים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An answer that relies on another rule only works if that other rule has a source. So the גמרא wants to find the root פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Themselves
From where do we know?

phrases.english: And sacrifices themselves, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the answer given in step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the age of קדשים is counted from the animal's birth

steps.title: 'A lamb in its year' means its own year
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב learns from 'כבש בן שנתו' that a sacrifice's year is its own year, not the calendar year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: The פסוק says 'a lamb in its year.' That means its own year, not a year counted by the world's calendar.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives the root source for קדשים: the word 'שנתו' (its year).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'its year', not just 'a year'. That small word tells us the year belongs to the animal and starts at its birth. This completes the source for דבי רב.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says
A lamb in its (first) year
The world's counting, the calendar year

steps.whatToRemember: According to דבי רב, the בכור's year counts from its birth because it follows all קדשים, and for קדשים we learn this from 'שנתו', its own year.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov said:
The verse states: "A lamb in its year"
its year means its own,
and not a year of the world's count.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 with a פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כבש בן שנתו' shows that a sacrifice's year is counted from its own birth

steps.title: Where does רב learn two days and one night?
steps.stepSummary: Since רב used 'שנה בשנה' for the counting of the year, the גמרא asks where he learns that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב: from where does he learn that the בכור is eaten for two days and one night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the question around to רב, and sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דבי רב learned the eating time from 'שנה בשנה'. רב used those words for something else, so he needs a different source for the two days and one night.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב, נֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד,
phrases.english: And Rav, that it is eaten for two days and one night,
from where does he derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב, נֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד, מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב's view from step 9 and asks the same kind of question as step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רב's source for the two-days-and-one-night eating time of a בכור

steps.title: רב learns it from the comparison to breast and thigh
steps.stepSummary: רב learns it from a פסוק that compares the meat of the בכור to the חזה ושוק of שלמים. Just as those are eaten for two days and one night, so is the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'And their meat shall be yours, like the breast of waving and like the right thigh.' The פסוק compares it to the חזה ושוק of שלמים. Just as there it is two days and one night, so too here it is two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב uses a הקש, a comparison the תורה makes by placing two things side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the בכור's meat says it is 'like' the חזה ושוק. The חזה ושוק come from שלמים, which may be eaten for two days and one night. So the בכור gets that same eating time, and רב no longer needs 'שנה בשנה' for this.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it (literally: it comes out for him)
Compared it (a הֶקֵּשׁ, a comparison made by the Torah)
Breast and thigh, the parts of שלמים given to the כהן
Peace offerings

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on both rules: the year counts from birth, and the eating time is two days and one night. They only disagree about which source teaches which rule.

phrases.english: He derives it from: "And their meat shall be yours,
like the breast of waving and like the right thigh"
The verse compared it
to the breast and thigh of a peace offering:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן שְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד,
phrases.english: just as there it is two days and one night,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן שְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד.
phrases.english: so too here it is two days and one night.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵ״וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וּכְשׁוֹק הַיָּמִין״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הקש to the חזה ושוק of שלמים gives the בכור an eating time of two days and one night
